title: I built an AI stock trader that is consistent
author: Dear_Station_75
selftext:
I built an AI stock trading agent from scratch, and I'm starting a series on it, what you need to know first, all the way through to how to build your own.



I've been running my own agent for over 4 months now, still 100% paper trading. My background before this was 5 years of trading stocks on my own, no coding background going in, so this has been a real crash course.



A few things I've learned along the way: writing a rule down and actually getting an AI to follow it in code are two very different things. I've found and fixed a long list of bugs over these 4 months, most of which took more than one attempt to actually get right. I audit every single trade it makes, every day, it's not something you set up once and walk away from.



The series is going to cover the whole build: the architecture, the rulebook, the bugs that taught me the most, and eventually the actual steps to build one yourself.



What would you like to learn about AI stock trading?

comments.author: profittoinvest
comments.body:
I agree with this a lot.

From our experience, AI can accelerate the whole process massively, but it can't replace actual trading knowledge. Without understanding how markets behave, it's very easy to build something that looks great in code or backtests and falls apart in live conditions.

The same applies to programming. You don't need to be a professional developer, but knowing the basics is extremely useful when debugging logic, checking whether the AI actually implemented the rule correctly, and spotting edge cases.

We've been developing our current trading system for over a year, and even though its behaviour is now much more predictable from an engineering and risk-management perspective, we still keep finding things worth improving and testing.

Good luck with your build — curious to see how it develops.
